target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Stop caching agent-default-derived model metadata on session entries so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: During every session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`), the resolved model was unconditionally written as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent turns, `resolveSessionModelRef` returned these cached fields directly, even after a config hot-reload changed the agent default. New child sessions inherited the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection`. Existing sessions (pre-fix) retained stale caches indefinitely.
- Solution: 
  1. **Reset (session-reset-service.ts)**: only cache modelProvider/model when the resolved model came from a user override — default-derived values are no longer persisted.
  2. **Resolver (session-utils.ts)**: when modelProvider/model are present without overrides and an agentId is available, compare against the current agent default: if they still match, return them directly (not stale); only when they differ are they treated as stale and re-resolved from the current config. This handles both pre-fix sessions (matching cache → preserved, stale cache → re-resolved) and avoids unnecessary re-resolution when the config hasn't changed.
  3. **Reset response (sessions.ts)**: include `resolvedModel` in the RPC response so the API always returns model info even when not stored.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (conditional cache), `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` (staleness detection), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (reset response), `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts` (override regression guard), `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` (new resolver tests)
- What did NOT change: Query-time behavior for sessions with explicit overrides; hot-reload handler; session persistence format

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but session model resolution keeps returning the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) was treated as authoritative over current config defaults. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session entries cache `modelProvider`/`model` from agent default during reset, and these become stale after a config hot-reload. Fix covers both new sessions (prevent caching) and existing sessions (fallback re-resolution).
- Real environment tested: Linux (Node 22.19), `fix/session-model-hot-reload-102269` branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-models.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run
  ```

- Behavioral matrix (resolveSessionModelRef — covers all paths):

  ```
  | Runtime modelProvider | Runtime model | Overrides | Config primary | Result |
  |----------------------|---------------|-----------|----------------|--------|
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (matches default, preserved) |
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (differs from default → stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (differs from default → stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | work-model     | openai/work-model | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 | openai/work-model (override preserved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | openai/gpt-5.4 (no agentId, backward compat) |
  ```

- Real behavior proof — live gateway hot-reload run:

  ```
  # Before: agents.defaults.model.primary = "zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B"
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "hi" --json
  → provider: "zte", model: "Qwen3-235B-A22B"

  # Change config: agents.defaults.model.primary = "zte/Qwen3-9999-TEST"
  $ openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary "zte/Qwen3-9999-TEST"

  # Gateway logs: config hot reload applied (agents.list)
  # No restart needed.

  # After: send another message
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "hi" --json
  → provider: "zte", model: "Qwen3-9999-TEST"   ← model changed!
  ```

- Unit/integration test evidence:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run

   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > prefers explicit session overrides ahead of...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves openrouter provider...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > falls back to override when runtime model is not recorded yet
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > keeps nested model ids...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves explicit wrapper providers...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > strips a duplicated provider prefix...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > falls back to resolved provider for unprefixed legacy runtime model
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves provider from slash-prefixed model...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > returns runtime metadata when it still matches...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves runtime metadata when agentId is not provided...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > re-resolves from current config when runtime metadata is stale (agentId, no overrides)

   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  488 passed (488)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts --run

   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  394 passed (394)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts --run

   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  268 passed (268)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-models.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run

   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  22 passed (22)
  ```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Live gateway hot-reload** — changing `agents.defaults.model.primary` and saving triggers hot-reload; next agent turn uses the new model immediately (shown above: Qwen3-235B-A22B → Qwen3-9999-TEST)
  2. **New sessions reset without user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` not cached → `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` → picks up current config
  3. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with matching cache** → `modelProvider`/`model` present and still match current default → returned directly (no unnecessary re-resolution)
  4. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with stale cache** → `modelProvider`/`model` differ from current default → re-resolved from current config
  5. **Sessions with user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` cached from override → override path takes precedence → non-default model preserved
  6. **Integration test** (non-default model with overrides) → unchanged (regression guard confirmed)
  7. **Reset RPC response** → includes `resolvedModel` field → clients always get model info
- What was not tested: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Reset with/without user overrides; override model preserved after reset; hot-reload picks up new default after reset
- Edge cases checked: Non-default `modelProvider`/`model` with overrides — preserved; without overrides — staleness check against current default (matching → preserved, differing → re-resolved); subagent sessions with fallback origin tracking — unchanged; explicit `model:null` patch — clears runtime metadata correctly; sessions.reset RPC response includes resolvedModel for all sessions
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `sessions.reset` response adds optional `resolvedModel` field (no breaking change); all 1172 tests pass across 5 related test files; pre-fix sessions get stale detection handled in resolver
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values). The query-time staleness detection compares cached values against current defaults to distinguish truly stale metadata from values that still match — avoiding unnecessary re-resolution when the config hasn't changed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: No remaining pre-fix session gap. Stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) on existing sessions is detected at query time by comparing against current defaults — matching values are preserved (no unnecessary re-resolution), differing values trigger re-resolution from current config. All sessions pick up the current config default on the next turn after hot-reload without waiting for a reset.
- **Mitigation**: Bounded and immediate. The resolver-side fix handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions without any migration, eager cleanup, or background invalidation.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All 1172 related tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path now compares runtime values against current defaults for the no-override + agentId case, but all observable behavior is preserved or improved.

---
